extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal. It evaluates the capacity of LLMs to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. The benchmark contains 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world scenarios (conference, organization, education, and game) across over 1373 webpages, in both Chinese and English. It includes both single-source and multi-source QAs with three difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard).
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages, constructing queries based on the provided page information, and verifying/filtering for legitimate queries. In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. Root pages are initially identified through Google searches using keywords such as 'conference official website' or 'game official website', followed by manual filtering. For the education domain, official websites of various university computer science departments are used.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Web pages' markdown content along with clickable HTML buttons (and corresponding URLs) are extracted using Beautiful Soup. The ai4crawl tool is used to get web pages in a Markdown-like format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-stage annotation: (1) LLM-based annotation with GPT-4o: Step 1 - Traverse official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages; Step 2 - Construct queries based on the provided page information and specified role, such as focusing on the solo page or considering both pages simultaneously; Step 3 - Verify and filter for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities. (2) Human Annotation: Human annotators rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human annotators verify and calibrate questions and answers generated by LLM to ensure correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowd-sourced human annotators (no further demographic details provided).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o for initial annotation; Beautiful Soup for HTML parsing; ai4crawl for webpage to Markdown conversion.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be available at HuggingFace Datasets. Code for WebWalker will be released on GitHub. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language (Chinese and English) is collected as part of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The domain distribution is uneven: conference (24.0%), organization (7.9%), education (46.3%), and game (24.0%). Language distribution: Chinese 60.5%, English 39.5%. The framework performs better in the conference domain due to more explicit and directive button information.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is relatively small (680 high-quality QA pairs) due to the complexity of web-agent queries. The work only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons without using visual modalities such as screenshots. Approximately 14k silver QA pairs exist but are not yet carefully human-verified.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website. Used as a benchmark for Testing/Validation. The ~14k silver QA pairs can serve as supplementary training data to enhance agent performance.
